items.definition:
express one's pleasure to (someone) at their success or good fortune
I want to congratulate you on your excellent exam results.

get rid of (someone or something) as no longer useful or desirable
Please discard all old newspapers in the recycling bin.

emit gas from the anus
He tried to hold it in, but he accidentally farted.

make a low, continuous, murmuring sound
The refrigerator began to hum loudly.

to observe and direct the execution of a task or activity
The manager supervises a team of ten employees.

to make fun of or provoke someone in a playful or unkind way
Don't tease your little brother.

to swipe
Please swipe your card to enter the building.

to reverse the effect of an action
I wish I could undo that mistake.

to become red in the face from embarrassment or shame
She would always blush when he complimented her.

to travel some distance regularly between one's home and place of work or study
He commutes to work by train every day.

to restore (something old, especially a building) to a good state of repair
They plan to renovate their old house next year.

to have the same sound at the end of words or lines
Do these two words rhyme?

to shine brightly with flashes of light
The diamonds on her necklace sparkled under the lights.

to form (fabric or a fabric item) by interlacing long threads passing in one direction with others at a right angle
The spider began to weave its web.

get rid of by throwing away or giving or selling to someone else
Please dispose of your trash properly.

achieve or realize (something desired, promised, or predicted)
He worked hard to fulfil his dreams.

to breathe in or out in short, quick breaths; to swell
He began to puff after running up the stairs.

dip (food) into a drink or sauce before eating it; score by forcing the ball down through the basket
He likes to dunk his cookies in milk.

to restart a computer system
Please reboot your computer to apply the updates.

to walk in a leisurely way
They went for a leisurely stroll in the park.

to entertain or make someone laugh
The clown tried to amuse the children with his tricks.

to continue firmly or obstinately
If you persist, you will eventually succeed.

to laugh quietly
He couldn't help but chuckle at the silly joke.

to make or become hard
The concrete will harden overnight.

to fill with air or gas; to increase in size or amount
We need to inflate the tires before the trip.

to make or become tight
Please tighten the screws on this shelf.

multiply
You need to multiply these numbers.

roam
The wild horses roam freely across the plains.

shorten
Can you shorten these trousers for me?

to boast
He likes to brag about his achievements.

eat grass; scrape skin
The cows graze in the field.

To wash and iron clothes; to conceal the origin of illegally obtained money.
She needs to launder her clothes this weekend.

open again
The store will reopen next Monday after renovations.

examine in detail
We need to analyse the data carefully.

to engage in conversation
They spent hours conversing about their travels.

crouch or sit with one's knees bent and one's heels close to or touching one's buttocks or the back of one's thighs
He had to squat down to pick up the dropped coin.

to write (something) again so as to alter or improve it
She had to rewrite her essay to improve the arguments.

to cry noisily
She began to sob uncontrollably.

to strike or bite with the beak or bill
The bird began to peck at the seeds on the ground.

to twist together into a confused mass
The fishing line got tangled in the weeds.

to take a quick, deep breath with your mouth open
She let out a gasp of surprise when she saw the gift.

to feel intense sorrow or distress
It takes time to grieve after losing a loved one.

To move quickly or awkwardly
The children scrambled over the rocks.

To concentrate on a particular area
He decided to specialise in criminal law.

To open or spread out
He watched the story unfold before his eyes.

to modify (something) to suit a particular individual or task
You can customize the settings to fit your preferences.

To move to a new place and establish one's home or business there
The company decided to relocate its headquarters to a different city.

To draw air audibly up the nose to detect a smell
The dog began to sniff the ground for clues.

to make or become wider
The road will widen after the bridge.

(of a person or animal) move from one area or country to another
Many birds migrate south for the winter.

make a long, low sound of pain, suffering, or pleasure
He let out a low moan of discomfort.

move in a circle on a central axis; consider something from all angles
The Earth revolves around the Sun.

fall suddenly, clumsily, or headlong
The child began to tumble down the stairs.

shed tears; cry
She began to weep silently after hearing the sad news.

hold (someone or something) close in one's arms as a way of showing affection or for comfort
The child wanted to cuddle with her teddy bear.

hear (someone or something) without meaning to or without the knowledge of the speaker
I couldn't help but overhear their conversation at the next table.

say or do something to remove the doubts or fears of someone
She tried to reassure him that everything would be fine.

charge (a battery or device) again; restore energy or vigor
I need to recharge my phone before we leave.

to rub against a rough surface, often causing damage or a harsh sound
He managed to scrape through the exam.

to cause to feel sudden shock or alarm
The loud noise startled the cat.

to look quickly and furtively
She tried to peep through the keyhole.

scatter or pour small drops or particles over an object or surface
Please sprinkle some cheese on top of the pasta.

ask for information from someone
She decided to inquire about the job opening.

plant (seed) by scattering it on or in the earth
Farmers sow seeds in the spring.
